claims.text: East New York Avenue & Remsen Avenue had 77 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 16 pedestrians injured, 8 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.3 million a year.
36% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.
Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading north in 31% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 19% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $142,000 a year.
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 4.2 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $1.4 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for East New York Avenue, Remsen Avenue (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 41, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 9.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 41, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 9
Subject: Request for safety study at East New York Avenue & Remsen Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write about the junction of East New York Avenue and Remsen Avenue to ask you to carry out a safety study and, on the roads you are responsible for, to consider timely fixes.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 147 crashes, of which 77 caused injury. Sixteen pedestrians and 8 cyclists were injured, and 1 person was killed. The location was listed among the city's priority locations for its safety record. No safety project is recorded in the period. In the U.S. DOT's official values (2024 dollars), the harm is about $5.3 million per year.

On East New York Avenue and Remsen Avenue, we ask you to assess:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent about 0.4 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about $142,000 in harm per year. In this city, where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

* longer yellow signal times, expected to prevent about 4.2 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,434,000 in harm per year, subject to a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and what measures will be taken.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
